title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A and B are small categories, e is the final category, and C^ denotes presheaves of sets on C. Grothendieck names each projection by the factor it kills. So p_B: A×B → A, p_A: A×B → B, q_A: A → e and q_B: B → e.

This generalises the previous page, which treated the case B = Δ (simplicial objects in A^). The page records the following.

(1) The currying equivalences (A×B)^ ≃ Hom(A°, B^) ≃ Hom(B°, A^).

(2) The direct images form a commutative square.
- (p_B)_*: (A×B)^ → A^ is X' ↦ Γ_B∘X', that is (p_B)_*X(a) = lim_{B°} X(a,−) = Hom(p_B^*h_a, X).
- Symmetrically, (p_A)_* is X'' ↦ Γ_A∘X''.
- q_{A*} = Γ_A = Hom_{A^}(e_{A^}, ·) and q_{B*} = Γ_B = Hom(e_{B^}, ·).
- q_A p_B = q_B p_A.

(3) Relative internal Homs are defined as direct images of the internal Hom of (A×B)^:
- Hom_A(X,Y) := p_{B*} Hom_{A×B}(X,Y), an object of A^;
- Hom_B(X,Y) := p_{A*} Hom_{A×B}(X,Y), an object of B^.
Taking global sections then gives Hom(X,Y) ≃ Γ_A Hom_A(X,Y) ≃ Γ_B Hom_B(X,Y).

(4) For b ∈ B, let Γ''_b: (A×B)^ → A^ be X ↦ X(−,b), i.e. evaluation at b after currying.
- Claim: Γ''_b(X) ≃ p_{B*} Hom(p_A^*(b), X) = Hom_A(p_A^*h_b, X), functorially in b and X.
- Proof by Yoneda: Hom_{A^}(a, p_{B*}Hom(p_A^*b, X)) ≃ Hom(p_B^*a, Hom(p_A^*b, X)) ≃ Hom(p_B^*a × p_A^*b, X).
- Since p_B^*h_a × p_A^*h_b = h_a ⊠ h_b = h_{(a,b)}, this is X(a,b). Hence 'OK'.
- The symmetric statement Γ'_a(X) ≃ p_{A*}Hom(p_B^*(a), X) for a ∈ A is written and then struck out ('likewise').

Purpose: this is the general form of formula I of the previous page, (Hom_A(L,X_n))_n = Hom_{A×Δ}(p_Δ^*L, X_*). That page is setting up the simplicial enrichment and cotensoring of simplicial presheaves (A×Δ)^ = Hom(Δ°, A^). It is groundwork for the closed-model-category discussion of the dossier, i.e. model structures on simplicial objects of a presheaf topos. The next sheet is reused computer printout dated 4 June 1982, consistent with 1982–83.
errors: Slip in the text: '(A×B)^ ≃ Hom(A°, B)' should read Hom(A°, B^).

Notation is fluid: the formula for Γ''_b is first written with subscripts later overwritten. The coherent version, matching the image, is p_{B*}Hom(p_A^*(b), X) with the Yoneda chain using p_B^*(a) × p_A^*(b). The machine transcription's p_{A*}Hom(p_B^*(b),X) is inconsistent with the stated conventions.
Otherwise the mathematics is correct and elementary.

ideas.what: Currying equivalence (A×B)^ ≃ Hom(A°,B^) ≃ Hom(B°,A^) and direct images along projections as fibrewise global sections (limits).
ideas.modern_name: Exponential law for presheaf categories; right Kan extension along a projection
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exposé I (presheaf topoi, functoriality of C^)

ideas.what: Relative internal Hom Hom_A(X,Y) := p_{B*}Hom_{A×B}(X,Y), with Hom = Γ_A Hom_A = Γ_B Hom_B.
ideas.modern_name: Relative / fibrewise internal Hom (enrichment of (A×B)^ over A^ or B^)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard topos theory (SGA4; enriched category theory)
ideas.where_published: Similar relative-Hom formalism appears in Les Dérivateurs and around Pursuing Stacks; unsure of an exact match

ideas.what: Evaluation at b: X(−,b) ≃ Hom_A(p_A^*h_b, X), proved via h_{(a,b)} = p_B^*h_a × p_A^*h_b and Yoneda.
ideas.modern_name: Evaluation as relative Hom out of a representable; external product of representables

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification of presheaf-category formalism (currying, relative internal Hom, evaluation via Yoneda). It generalises the previous page's computation for simplicial presheaves and contains no new result or connection. Its only interest is as context for the dossier's closed-model work around 1982–83.
transcription_corrections: The formula for Γ''_b should read Γ''_b(X) ≃ p_{B*} Hom(p_A^*(b), X) (≃ Hom_A(p_A^*(b), X)), not p_{A*}Hom(p_B^*(b),X).
In the Yoneda chain: Hom_{A^}(a, p_{B*}Hom(p_A^*(b),X)) ≃ Hom_{(A×B)^}(p_B^*(a), Hom(p_A^*(b),X)) ≃ Hom_{(A×B)^}(p_B^*(a)×p_A^*(b), X).
'(A×B)^ ≃ Hom(A°, B)' is as written in the manuscript, but is a slip for B^.
The final line under the struck block reads something like 'id. avant' / 'cf. avant'; it is uncertain.
